body.statement:
For each \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\}\), there are pairs
\[
(P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\subset\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)
\]
such that \(P_{\ell,q}(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\mid E_0)\ge c_X\), their conditional joint observed-data testing affinity is uniformly bounded away from zero,
\[
\inf_{N,T,\mathbf n}\int\min\{dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q}\}>0,
\]
and
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,q}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,q}}(z_0)|^2\ge cR_q
\quad\text{on }\mathcal Z_+.
\]
The treated-mean, replicated-smoothing, and donor pairs may additionally be chosen with uniformly bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence.  For the random-spacing pair only positive testing affinity is asserted.  Every pair is induced by a regular conditional law of the complete causal panel.  In particular, its observed event outcomes have conditional means stable given the complete historical design, and its historical errors are centered conditional on that design.
body.justification: All four pairs are completed as causal panels in the full-design-centered subclass, with the two strong conditional-mean restrictions verified directly.
body.gap: The spacing experiment is certified by positive testing affinity on a no-design-point event; bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence is deliberately not claimed for it.
body.consumer: The minimax and interval lower bounds therefore apply to the causal panel experiment rather than an auxiliary fixed-query kernel.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,1\le t\le T\}\).  We construct all experiments conditional on a fixed value of \(E_0\).  The query is chosen in a fixed compact subset of the interior of \(([0,1]^d)^S\), and \(\mathcal Z_+\) is chosen to contain that compact set; hence the displayed positive-query probability is one.  Historical coordinates are i.i.d. with a density between the prescribed fixed bounds.  Conditional on \(\mathscr X\), historical responses are independent across units and dates, are supported in \([0,B]\), and have means \(m_s(X_{st})\).  Their Bernoulli probabilities are kept in a fixed subinterval of \((0,1)\), so their conditional variances are bounded below by \(B^{-1}\) after choosing the fixed scale within the nonempty compatibility range of the class constants.  Event outcomes are bounded and independent across units and of \(\mathscr X\).  Unobserved event-date untreated potential outcomes are completed with cohort-average conditional mean \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  Consistency, historical consistency, no spillovers, limited anticipation, and event transport then hold.  Moreover,
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\]
Thus every construction below satisfies the two defining restrictions of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).  Independent calendar coordinates have zero conditional \(\beta\)-mixing coefficients.  The donor variables are independent of the panel, i.i.d. conditional on \(E_0\), and are chosen with covariance eigenvalues in \([c_\Sigma,C_\Sigma]\) and standardized fourth moment at most \(B\).  Exact training coordinates are obtained by setting \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).

We use one elementary Bernoulli bound repeatedly.  If \(p,p+v\in[\eta,1-\eta]\), then Taylor's theorem applied to the Bernoulli relative entropy gives
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p+v,p)
\le \frac{v^2}{2\eta(1-\eta)}.
\tag{1}
\]
Also, for product experiments, direct expansion of the log likelihood ratio gives additivity of Kullback--Leibler divergence.

For the treated channel, put
\[
V_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
\]
and change the event Bernoulli mean in cohort \(s\) by
\[
v_s=c_0\frac{\pi_s}{n_sV_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}},
\]
where \(c_0>0\) is fixed sufficiently small.  Since \(S\) and the weights are fixed and \(n_s\to\infty\), all probabilities remain in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).  The target separation is
\[
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_sv_s
=c_0V_{\mathrm{tr}}^{-1/2}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
=c_0R_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}.
\tag{2}
\]
By (1), the divergence of all event observations is at most
\[
C\sum_{s=1}^{S}n_sv_s^2=Cc_0^2.
\tag{3}
\]
All other observed variables have the same law.  Taking \(c_0\) small makes the testing affinity uniformly positive.

For the smoothing channel choose \(s_*\) maximizing
\[
\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}.
\]
Because \(S\) is fixed, this maximum is at least \(R_{\mathrm{sm}}/S\).  Put
\[
b=(Tn_{s_*})^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}
\]
and let \(\psi\) be a fixed compactly supported \(\lambda\)-Holder bump with \(\psi(0)=1\).  Perturb only the \(s_*\)-surface by
\[
m_{s_*,1}(x)-m_{s_*,0}(x)=c_1b^\lambda
\psi\!\left(\frac{x-z_{0s_*}}b\right).
\tag{4}
\]
The constant \(c_1\) is chosen small enough that both surfaces remain in the Holder ball, in the response interior, and within the same two-sided local-modulus bounds; a common affine carrier is used when \(\lambda>1\), and a common one-sided \(\lambda\)-cusp carrier is used when \(0<\lambda\le1\).  These carriers have respectively modulus exponents one and \(\lambda\), hence exponent \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).  Formula (4) gives target separation
\[
c_1\pi_{s_*}b^\lambda,
\qquad
c_1^2\pi_{s_*}^2b^{2\lambda}\ge \frac{c}{S}R_{\mathrm{sm}}.
\tag{5}
\]
Only a set of design probability at most \(Cb^d\) is perturbed.  Applying (1), integrating over the design, and summing over \(Tn_{s_*}\) responses gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{sm}},P_{0,\mathrm{sm}})
\le C Tn_{s_*}b^{2\lambda+d}=C.
\tag{6}
\]

For the spacing channel take \(h=c_2T^{-1/d}\) and use the same local perturbation as in (4), now with bandwidth \(h\), in any fixed cohort with positive weight.  Choose its support ball \(A_h\) so that \(P(X_{st}\in A_h\mid E_0)\le Cc_2^d/T\).  On
\[
\mathcal A_h=\{X_{st}\notin A_h\text{ for every }t\},
\]
the complete observed conditional response kernels under the two laws coincide.  Independence of the calendar coordinates yields
\[
P(\mathcal A_h\mid E_0)
\ge\left(1-\frac{Cc_2^d}{T}\right)^T
\ge c'>0
\tag{7}
\]
for sufficiently small fixed \(c_2\).  Hence the overlap integral of the two joint laws is at least \(c'\).  Their target separation is a fixed positive multiple of
\[
h^\lambda=T^{-\lambda/d},
\tag{8}
\]
whose square is \(R_{\mathrm{sp}}\).  This argument uses the no-design-point event and asserts no bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence.

For the donor channel take a globally affine carrier when \(\lambda>1\), and a globally defined asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp carrier when \(0<\lambda\le1\).  Scale it so that its covariance-standardized weighted modulus lies between \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^\kappa\) and \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^\kappa\) throughout the declared interior radius.  There is then a covariance-standardized direction \(u_N\) with
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2=c_3N^{-1/2}le\delta_0
\]
and
\[
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{N,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\ge cN^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{9}
\]
Under the two laws let the donor observations have a common bounded, smooth location-family density with covariance \(\Sigma\), means respectively \(z_0\) and \(z_0+u_N\), and finite standardized fourth moment within the declared envelope.  Choosing the fixed location family with finite Fisher information and expanding its log density, or directly using a Gaussian carrier when the fourth-moment envelope permits it, gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{don}},P_{0,\mathrm{don}})
\le CN\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^2
=Cc_3^2.
\tag{10}
\]
Keep the observed event mean fixed and complete the unobserved untreated event outcome under each law with mean \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  The identifying formula then makes (9) exactly the target separation, whose square is at least \(cN^{-\kappa}=cR_{\mathrm{don}}\).

For the three bounded-divergence experiments, let \(A=\{dP_1/dP_0\ge1\}\), put \(p=P_1(A)\), and put \(q=P_0(A)\).  The log-sum inequality, obtained by applying Jensen's inequality separately on \(A\) and \(A^c\), gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)
\ge p\log\frac pq+(1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1-q}
\ge2(p-q)^2,
\]
where the final inequality follows by differentiating the binary relative entropy twice in \(p\).  Since \(p-q=\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\) and \(\int\min(dP_0,dP_1)=1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\),
\[
\int\min(dP_0,dP_1)
\ge1-\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2}.
\]
The perturbation constants in (2), (4), and (9) can be reduced so that the right-hand side is a fixed positive number.  Equation (7) supplies the corresponding affinity directly for spacing.  The causal completions preceding (1) verify all panel-law conditions, including the two full-design restrictions, and complete the proof.
